Jodi also shares other challenging moments in her life that strengthened her faith and trust in God, leading her to the work and mission she’s tackling now.

🔔 Ethereum price breakout hinges on a close above $2,535 

➡️ Ethereum price hovered around $2,500 on Sep. 9 as buyers defended short-term support, but weakening momentum and negative capital flows kept a breakout above $2,535 out of reach. Ethereum price traded near $2,486 at the time of writing on Sep. 9 after briefly rising above $2,520 earlier in the session. Price remained almost unchanged on the daily chart as buyers and sellers competed around the psychological $2,500 level.

🔖 The narrow move followed several days of consolidation after ETH recovered from its early-September low near $2,430. Buyers have repeatedly stepped in around $2,478–$2,485, but each attempt to extend the recovery has met selling pressure between $2,525 and $2,535.Spot Ethereum exchange-traded fund outflows have reduced one source of institutional demand during the consolidation. Broader risk appetite has also remained weak ahead of the Federal Reserve’s Sep. 15–16 policy meeting, while higher energy prices linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict have added to inflation concerns.

⚠️ Regulatory uncertainty ahead of the expected U.S. Senate procedural vote on the Clarity Act on Sep. 15 has given institutional investors another reason to limit exposure. Ethereum has consequently struggled to separate from the wider risk-off tone across the crypto market.

📄 Envoy says IAEA BoG resolution not effective

📌 London, IRNA — Iran’s permanent ambassador to the United Nations and other international organizations in Vienna, Reza Najafi, has criticized Western nations for politicizing the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Board of Governors and stressed that there wouldn’t be any actual effect from this resolution.

“Well, we have a very principled position. We will continue to protect our national interests by all means. For a reaction to this resolution, we will follow the same principle,” Najafi told CGTN on Saturday.
​
“We should see what would be the actual effects of such a resolution. In our view, there wouldn't be any actual effect by this resolution. But we will assess, and based on our assessment, we will react to that,” he added.
​
“The access to all facilities existed before the attack, and it was the attack and the aggression against Iran which caused the current situation,” he noted.
​
“So Iran should not be blamed for that. And claiming that Iran is not cooperating or breaching an obligation is technically and legally wrong and a false assumption,” he stated.
​
The IAEA Board of Governors had approved a resolution proposed by the United States and three European countries, Britain, France, and Germany, with 23 votes in favor, three against, and eight abstentions. Russia, China, and Niger voted against the resolution.
​
The resolution, which repeats political allegations regarding Iran’s peaceful nuclear activities, calls on the IAEA Director General to refer Iran’s case to both the UN Security Council and the General Assembly.
​
Earlier, in an explanatory note submitted in response to the latest report by IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, Iran’s mission to the agency had pushed back against expectations for routine implementation of safeguards, arguing that such demands are unreasonable given the continued threats and hostilities targeting the country.
​
